【POSE】

【HEAD DIRECTION & FACIAL ORIENTATION】
The head direction and facial orientation must strictly follow Image 2.

Match the exact direction in which the head is turned or tilted, including:

* facing directly toward the camera
* looking to the left or right
* looking upward or downward
* three-quarter head orientation
* profile orientation
* head tilt
* chin position

Do not automatically make the person face the camera. If the face in Image 2 is turned away from the camera, reproduce that orientation.

The facial orientation must remain naturally connected to the neck and body, with anatomically correct head rotation and perspective.

【GAZE DIRECTION】
The person's eye direction must also follow Image 2.

Match whether the subject is:

* looking directly at the camera
* looking to the left or right
* looking upward or downward
* looking away from the camera

Do not force eye contact with the camera if Image 2 does not show eye contact.

【FACIAL EXPRESSION】
The facial expression must strictly follow Image 2 while preserving the person's facial identity from Image 1.

Match the expression shown in Image 2, including:

* neutral expression
* slight smile
* natural smile
* serious expression
* relaxed expression
* surprised expression
* subtle emotional expression
* mouth shape
* lip position
* eyebrow position
* eye openness
* eyelid shape
* cheek tension
* overall facial muscle tension

Do not simply copy the face from Image 2. Preserve the identity, facial structure, and recognizable features of Image 1, while reproducing the expression and emotional state shown in Image 2.

【SHOT SCALE / FRAMING】
The shot scale must strictly follow Image 2. Do not preserve the original framing or shot scale from Image 1.

Match Image 2 in terms of:

* camera distance
* subject size within the frame
* framing
* cropping position
* visible portion of the body
* headroom
* body placement within the frame

If Image 2 is an extreme close-up, output an extreme close-up.
If Image 2 is a close-up, output a close-up.
If Image 2 is a medium shot, output a medium shot.
If Image 2 is a half-body shot, output a half-body shot.
If Image 2 is a 7/8-body shot, output a 7/8-body shot.
If Image 2 is a full-body shot, output a full-body shot.

The person's scale and cropping within the frame must closely match Image 2.

【CAMERA ANGLE / VIEWPOINT】
The camera angle and viewpoint must strictly follow Image 2. Do not retain the original camera angle from Image 1.

Accurately match Image 2 in terms of:

* camera viewing direction
* front / side / rear / three-quarter view
* left-right camera orientation
* horizontal viewing angle
* eye-level / high-angle / low-angle perspective
* camera elevation
* perspective relationship between the subject and camera
* subject orientation relative to the camera

If Image 2 shows a frontal view, use a frontal view.
If Image 2 shows a side view, use the corresponding side view.
If Image 2 shows a rear view, use a rear view.
If Image 2 shows a three-quarter or angled view, precisely reproduce that viewpoint.

The body, head, and face must naturally adapt to the new camera viewpoint with physically correct perspective and anatomy.

【FINAL RESULT】

Create a photorealistic image combining the person and background from Image 1 with the exact pose, head direction, facial orientation, gaze direction, facial expression, shot scale, framing, and camera viewpoint from Image 2, using Image 3 only as skeletal guidance.

The final image should look as if the person from Image 1 was originally photographed in the exact pose, viewpoint, framing, head direction, gaze direction, and facial expression shown in Image 2.

Do not alter the person's identity, facial structure, hairstyle, body proportions, clothing, accessories, or background.
